title: With fixedTimeLimit, a non-Exception/non-Error callable Throwable reaches retry predicates as ExecutionException; retryIfExceptionOfType stops matching
cause: AttemptTimeLimiters.FixedAttemptTimeLimit.call delegates to Guava's deprecated SimpleTimeLimiter.callWithTimeout(callable, d, u, true); its throwCause rethrows the cause only if it is an Exception or Error and otherwise rethrows the outer FutureTask ExecutionException (SimpleTimeLimiter.java:261-268 in Guava 22.0). Retryer.call records that wrapper as the attempt's exception, and ExceptionClassPredicate/ExceptionPredicate classify Attempt.getExceptionCause() without unwrapping, so the predicates see java.util.concurrent.ExecutionException instead of the callable's throwable.
trigger: A Retryer built with AttemptTimeLimiters.fixedTimeLimit (either factory) and retryIfExceptionOfType(T)/retryIfException(Predicate)/retryIfException() runs a callable that throws a Throwable subclass that is neither Exception nor Error (e.g. via commons-lang3 ExceptionUtils.rethrow, Lombok @SneakyThrows, Class.newInstance, or Kotlin/Groovy/Scala code). No timeout is needed.
consequence: With retryIfExceptionOfType(T.class) or a Predicate<Throwable> matching T, Retryer.call stops after 1 invocation and throws ExecutionException(ExecutionException(t)) instead of retrying and throwing RetryException(cause=t) as it does without a time limit; with retryIfException() the non-Exception throwable is retried instead (3 invocations, RetryException(cause=ExecutionException(t))). Listeners and RetryException see ExecutionException as the attempt's cause.
premises: Guava provides the 4-argument SimpleTimeLimiter.callWithTimeout used by FixedAttemptTimeLimit (Guava 22.0 and earlier; reproduced with 22.0, 16.0.1, 14.0.1 and 10.0.1), whose throwCause rethrows the outer ExecutionException when the cause is neither an Exception nor an Error (SimpleTimeLimiter.java:261-268 in 22.0).
The user callable throws a Throwable that is neither an Exception nor an Error; the time limit does not expire.
guava-retrying applies no unwrapping between AttemptTimeLimiter.call and the rejection predicate (Retryer.call catch(Throwable) -> ExceptionAttempt -> getExceptionCause).
